statement: Settings and remapped controls are written to two files in the player's folder, but no test restarts the game on Windows or on a Steam Deck to show they survive, and a failed write is silently ignored.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (one scripted save, quit, start, read test run on two exports)
risk: A Deck's file layout or a read-only folder drops a tester's comfort settings each start; seen early by running the round trip on the first Linux export.

statement: The checks that plan every screen at 1280 by 800 exist but run in no CI job, and no saved record or set of stills shows the menus free of clipped or overlapping text at the Deck's size.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (the planning check exists; the work is a saved run per candidate and a stills sweep through the guarded capture launcher)
risk: A menu added late (horde, custom planet, the new side-rail menus) clips on the Deck and nobody sees it until a tester does; seen early by making the sweep a per-candidate record.

statement: There is no accessibility pass or record newer than 2026-10-31 and no runs folder for the area, so the accessibility items of the 'before an outside tester plays' list do not exist as a list.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (a re-read of ten items against the candidate, written as a checklist with a record)
risk: The 2026-10-28 summary still says no volume controls and no text size, which is no longer true, so the team plans from a stale page; seen early by dating the checklist to the candidate's commit.

statement: The Hit pause slider is still shown on the Accessibility page and still has no reader outside the user interface, so moving it changes nothing (corrective item CD-14, open).
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (hide one row, or wire it when hit-stop lands)
risk: Wiring it into the sim's hit-stop instead of hiding it would change the state hash and need a golden window; seen early by deciding hide or wire first.

statement: Sounds are captioned for two cues only (the beam struggle and an opening), and that caption line is off by default, so a player who cannot hear gets no words for other sound cues.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (a caption word per sound family, then hud_check rows)
risk: Captions for a fast fight can flood the bottom edge; seen early by capping to one line and testing on a saved match.

statement: Corrective item CD-14 has an empty progress cell and no commit or record names it since 2026-11-07, although one of its four parts (a brace button on pads) is in fact done on the Arena layout.
risk: An open corrective row with no state hides which parts still need work; seen early by filling the row.

statement: The Simple controller layout binds no brace button, so whether the 'Button only' brace style leaves a Simple-layout player without a brace is not evidenced.
risk: The option the game offers as the easier one could remove a defence on the easier layout; one input test on the Simple layout settles it.

statement: Nothing written says the Alpha is English only, the game has no language choice, and the translation tools and the stretched-text test copy run in no CI job.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (one line in the tester guide now; translation is after Alpha)
risk: A tester expects another language; seen early by saying English only on the download page.
orb_question: Is the Alpha English only? Recommended: yes, and say so in the tester guide.

statement: On main the switch that stops Reduce flashing being turned off is false, and no record shows a tester build of the baseline made with it on; the tool step that sets it exists.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (the lock step exists; the gap is a recorded verify on the candidate)
risk: An outside tester's build ships unlocked; seen early by the package verify's locked check on every candidate.

statement: There is no screen reader or menu narration: the area's own audit found no text-to-speech call, and a search of ui/ and render/ at the baseline finds none.
risk: None for Alpha; say so in the tester guide.

statement: Colour-blind mode (three presets) is an option that reaches the HUD, the fighters' colours and the effects.
Text size has three steps and every text goes through one function with a 14-pixel floor, above the 9 the specification proposed.
Hold-or-toggle exists per player for energy, guard, the manoeuvre and charging stances and transform, and the host passes each to the input layer.
A Simple controller layout and a remap screen exist, and remapped controls are saved to the player's folder.
Each change on the Settings screen is saved at once and applied at the next start, and the HUD check that covers this passed on the baseline's game code (8288 checks, 0 failed).
Master, effects and voice volume and mono sound are options with a reader in the audio code.
Reduce flashing defaults to on, the start notice can be re-read from the Accessibility page, and a lock that forces the option on is built into the settings code.
